beliefs.practice: Load the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime, never hard-code or check the secret into source control, and do not log the full URI; use a .env.example with a placeholder instead.

Open the Mongoose/Mongo driver with explicit modern options: useNewUrlParser: true, useUnifiedTopology: true, serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 5000, socketTimeoutMS: 600000, maxPoolSize: 50 and set an appName; include retryWrites=true in the connection string if supported.

When using change streams, call watch() with fullDocument: 'updateLookup' if your alert evaluation needs the full current document, persist the latest resumeToken to durable storage after each processed change, and on restart try to resume using that token (with exponential backoff and jitter if resume fails).

Keep change-stream handlers short and nonblocking: push webhook delivery and heavy alert evaluation to a background worker or message queue so the watch loop can acknowledge/resume quickly and avoid large event-processing latencies or timeouts.

Design alert rule documents so they can be looked up by assetId (or symbol) and active flag; create a compound index on { assetId: 1, active: 1 } so the change-stream handler can quickly find only relevant rules for an updated position rather than scanning all rules.

Add indexes to support your aggregation match stages—e.g., for portfolio P&L and sector allocation create indexes on { accountId: 1 }, { symbol: 1 }, and { sector: 1 } (or a compound index { accountId: 1, symbol: 1 }) so $match and $group stages run without full-collection scans; build indexes idempotently via a script.

Use aggregation options allowDiskUse: true for potentially large portfolio aggregations, and limit aggregation pipeline result shapes and projections so documents transferred over the wire are minimal; test aggregate with realistic dataset sizes.

Make webhook delivery idempotent: include an event id (change _id or resume token) and have the webhook receiver deduplicate, or persist a short-lived delivery record on the service side so retries won't produce duplicate actions.

Implement retry with exponential backoff and jitter for transient MongoNetworkError/MongoServerSelectionError and for webhook delivery; cap retries and surface permanent failures to an operator queue or dead-letter store.
Make seeding/idempotent: seed scripts should upsert by a stable natural key (e.g., symbol+accountId for positions, ruleId for alert rules) so they can be run repeatedly without creating duplicates.

Avoid opening many separate connections or one change stream per user; run a single shared change-stream watcher (per process) and fan-out events internally or partition by logical key if you must scale horizontally; tune maxPoolSize to match concurrency.

Model embeddings for vector search as a fixed-length array of floats under a named field (e.g., embedding: [Number]), store the vector dimensionality explicitly in the schema, and normalize vectors client-side if using cosine similarity so index/search behave predictably.

Create a dedicated vector index with explicit parameters (indexType: 'HNSW' or 'IVF', similarity: 'cosine' or 'dot', dimensions: N, efConstruction and M for HNSW) via the cluster's index API or createIndex extension rather than relying on a default B-tree index for embedding fields.
Use schema-level projections and .lean() in read-heavy aggregation and query helpers (Mongoose) to avoid building full Mongoose documents when you only need plain objects for aggregation/evaluation.

Instrument and monitor latency, server selection, connection pool metrics, and slow queries; on Azure enable Diagnostic Settings / Azure Monitor for the cluster and capture MongoDB slow query logs and server metrics so you can correlate alerts triggered by data with database performance.

Choose provisioned throughput (or autoscale) to cover peak workloads from the change-stream watcher and occasional large aggregations; for Cosmos-based services configure RU/s or autoscale so long-running aggregations won't be throttled, and design aggregations to run during off-peak windows if necessary.

Handle common server errors by code: on resumable change-stream errors or transient rollback codes implement resume/retry; treat AuthenticationFailure as non-retriable until credentials are rotated; surface unrecoverable errors to ops with diagnostic context (resume token, last processed _id).

Back up critical collections (positions, alertrules) regularly and ensure your backup/restore process preserves resumeTokens if you need point-in-time replay; enable the platform backup (continuous or periodic) offered by Azure for production.

Write unit tests for aggregation logic with realistic sample documents and include a short integration test that runs the aggregation against the live sample_fintech_03 database to validate index usage and pipeline performance.

Ensure alert rule evaluation is near-constant-time per rule by precomputing thresholds and using numeric comparisons; avoid expensive lookups in the hot path—cache static lookups like instrument metadata (sector, multiplier) with TTL in-memory or a fast cache.
